mathematics.statement: For a quasi-compact morphism f:X->Y, dominance is equivalent to every generic point y of an irreducible component of Y having a source irreducible-component generic point in its fibre.
mathematics.disposition: reviewed_existing; whole proposition covered by composition; no full-statement single-tag equivalence claimed
generic_preimage_upgrade: 01RL gives an arbitrary preimage x of each target component generic point y.
004W supplies an irreducible component C of X containing x.
01IS supplies the generic point eta of C.
Continuity gives y=f(x) in closure{f(eta)}, hence closure{y} is contained in closure{f(eta)}.
The first closure is an irreducible component of Y and the second is irreducible, so maximality gives equality.
01IS gives uniqueness of their generic point, hence f(eta)=y.
mathematics.sufficiency: 01RK applies without quasi-compactness and only requires an arbitrary preimage of each target component generic point.
mathematics.proof_route: 01K4 supplies finite affine covers. The French proof chooses a chart whose image closure contains y and reduces source and target; 01RL instead uses the finite affine disjoint union. 00FL gives dense-image/kernel-consisting-of-nilpotent-elements/minimal-prime-image equivalence; reduced target implies injectivity. 0CAN then lifts each minimal target prime in the image to a minimal source prime.
mathematics.citation_boundary: 01RL explicitly invokes 00FL and the finite disjoint-union-of-affines lemma. 01RK explicitly invokes 004W and 01IS. 01K4 and 0CAN are supplemental reconstruction edges, not represented as direct citations in 01RL; 00FL does not directly cite 0CAN.
mathematics.hypothesis_boundary: Quasi-compactness is retained for necessity. The preimage upgrade and sufficiency require none. Reducedness and affineness belong only to proof reductions. No integrality finite-type Noetherianity or separation condition is introduced.
